title: Single-site deletion kept four ozone by moisture slope signs in eastern US forest injury samples in 1994-2010
abstract: We tested whether one forest site determined an annual ozone by soil moisture slope. We used a published panel with 5,277 site-years in four Northeast and North Central US samples in 1994-2002 and 2003-2010. A fixed model controlled site, year, curved exposure terms, visit date and plant and species counts. None of 914 single-site deletions changed the slope sign. In contrast, removing the highest-weight five percent of sites changed the early North Central slope from +0.113 to -0.034 injury probability per 10 ppm-h ozone per moisture SD. Half the residual design weight came from 11.3-16.6 percent of sites. Thus record-level concentration did not imply dependence on one site. These are descriptive sensitivity tests with the same source data as prior campaign studies. The prior uncertainty intervals included zero. Coarse exposure, unknown missed injury and shared weather patterns limit biological interpretation. Code, aggregate checks, a figure and exact external retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Cumulative partial design weights across sites and exact single-site deletion ranges. Lines are sensitivity ranges, not confidence intervals. The orange marks remove the top five percent of sites ranked by design weight.
